summary.summary: PROVED (with one standard real-algebraic step ASSUMED for locality): (a) a finite-reach coupling's response is conserved on every stationary state iff its symbol has no block between equal energies, and then, the walk squaring to a scalar, it is i[H, G] with G = -i(H'A + AH)/(|s(k + p)|^2 - |s(k)|^2); Delta is irreducible and square-free over Q(i), so G is local, of reach one less than the coupling (exact for blocks 63 and 69 at a plane wave); (b) hence no local coupling on Z^3 needs a non-local generator; (c) curl couplings are conserved identically, make no lengths and leave block 72's requirement unchanged; (d) for every coupling of reach <= 2 the mean over the eight species of the shear metric they see is exactly zero - one geometry for all species needs reach three, whatever the generator - so no reach-two coupling meets the ladder's demands (no HIT by the task's criterion)

Its N1.1 leaves couplings of other kinds. (a) Let dH[B] be a hermitian deformation of the walk, linear in a bond field B_a^j, of finite reach and translation-covariant. Suppose its response d<H>/dB is lattice-divergence-free on EVERY stationary state of the walk (that is what block 64 T1 needs). Show that then dH[d xi] has vanishing diagonal blocks in the walk's eigenspaces for every xi, hence dH[d xi] = i[H, G_xi] for some G_xi; then decide whether G_xi can always be chosen LOCAL (finite reach, linear in xi, of the form sum_x xi_j(x) rho_j(x)), using the walk's explicit spectrum (energies +-|s(k)|, eight zeros): the obstruction is a division by energy differences; on the torus work it out exactly for xi a single plane wave of wave vector p. (b) If a non-local G exists for some local dH, give the smallest example and test it against the ladder's four demands (exact current; one geometry for all species; the energy reversal by U_(111); block 72's requirement for every species). (c) Couplings through the curls alone: show that their response is conserved identically and that they make no lengths for uniform strains; do they change block 72's requirement? (d) Conclude with a theorem for all finite-reach couplings, or an explicit reach-two coupling that meets all four demands. HIT if such a reach-two coupling exists.
